[[Category:Measure theory| 1]]
Let $X=\{x_i\}$ be a [[set]] of points, $\mathcal{F}(X)$ be any of its [[sigma algebra]], then

$$
(X,\mathcal{F}(X))
$$

is a [[measurable space]], where $F \in \mathcal{F}(X)$ are called '''measurable sets'''.


== Special case: Countable sample space ==

For [[cardinality|countable]] sample spaces, one usually takes

$$
\mathcal F=\mathcal P(X),
$$
where $\mathcal{P}$ is the [[power set]] of $X$.
